workflow_start_instructions.description: How to start the reflow workflow for a new system or system-of-systems
setup_steps: 1. Create a folder in ./systems/ with your system name (e.g., systems/my_system/)
2. Inside the system folder, create a text document describing your system or system-of-systems requirements
3. Tell your LLM agent: 'Run the decision_flow.json workflow on system <system_name>'
4. The workflow will automatically look in systems/<system_name>/ and guide you through the process
workflow_start_instructions.system_location: All systems must be located in the ./systems/ directory
workflow_start_instructions.workflow_discovery: The decision flow automatically detects and works with systems in the systems/ folder

NEVER_LOCATIONS: NEVER in specs/, services/, or docs/ directories

WORKING_DIRECTORY_REQUIREMENT.rule: LLM agent MUST cd to systems/<system_name>/ at the start of EVERY workflow step
WORKING_DIRECTORY_REQUIREMENT.relative_paths: Once in correct directory, use relative paths: context/current_focus.md, context/dev_progress_tracker.json
WORKING_DIRECTORY_REQUIREMENT.common_error: If you cannot find tracking files, you are in the WRONG DIRECTORY - immediately run pwd and cd to correct location

rag_enhanced_mode.description: RAG-enhanced context management provides semantic retrieval and automatic injection of relevant workflow context

mcp_integration.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized interface for LLM agents to discover resources, invoke tools, and get prompt templates
setup_instructions: 1. Install MCP SDK: pip install mcp
2. Configure MCP client with server path and reflow root
4. LLM agents can now use MCP protocol for all reflow interactions
benefits: Resource discovery via MCP URIs (reflow://system/{name}/context/memory)
Type-safe tool invocation with JSON Schema validation
Pre-formatted prompt templates (critical_behavioral_rules, step_start_context)
Standardized access works with any MCP-compatible LLM client
Server manages state (current system) automatically
Structured error handling instead of parsing shell output
mcp_integration.integration_with_rag: MCP provides standardized access layer, RAG provides intelligent context retrieval. Use together for optimal workflow adherence.

NEVER_GENERATE_REPORTS: NEVER generate a report after completing a step or substep
NEVER summarize what you just did unless explicitly requested by user
NEVER create 'status update' or 'progress report' documents
NEVER output commentary about the work completed
ONLY update tracking files (working_memory.json, step_progress_tracker.json, process_log.md) - no reports
After completing work: UPDATE tracking files, then STOP. No explanation. No summary. No report.
MANDATORY_WORKFLOW_ADHERENCE: READ decision_flow.json AND current workflow step file BEFORE every action
VERIFY current step/substep from step_progress_tracker.json matches decision_flow instructions
DO NOT proceed with actions that contradict decision_flow.json - even if they seem helpful
DO NOT skip steps or substeps defined in workflow files
DO NOT reinterpret workflow instructions - follow them EXACTLY as written
If decision_flow.json says 'do X', you MUST do X. Not Y. Not X plus helpful extras. Just X.
Context does NOT refresh between steps - decision_flow.json instructions are ALWAYS active
NEVER assume decision_flow.json guidance is 'optional' or 'advisory' - it is MANDATORY
CONTEXT_CONTINUITY: Decision flow instructions persist across ALL interactions until workflow completion
You MUST re-read decision_flow.json if you detect yourself violating its instructions
step_progress_tracker.json is the ONLY source of truth for current position in workflow
working_memory.json contains MANDATORY context that must be consulted before every action
If you feel uncertain about next action: READ step_progress_tracker.json, READ current_focus.md, READ decision_flow.json, THEN act

cross_contamination_prevention: NEVER reference or modify files in other system directories
All file paths must be relative to current system directory or absolute with verified system_name
Before reading ANY file, verify it contains the current system_name in its path
If you find yourself in wrong system directory, STOP immediately and return to correct directory
NEVER copy files between system directories
NEVER reference service architectures from other systems in dependencies
ALL context files must be read from current system directory only
Verify system_name in working_memory.json matches pwd before every file operation
system_isolation.context_file_location: ALL context files (current_focus.md, working_memory.json, etc.) MUST be in systems/<system_name>/context/
system_isolation.sanity_check: If system_name from working_memory.json doesn't match pwd, ERROR and STOP

operation_counter_definition.description: Precise definition of what counts as an operation for context refresh trigger
counts_as_operation: File modified (1 per file, excluding tracking files)
Service switched in multi-service workflow (1 count)
Major decision made and documented (1 count)
does_not_count: Updating tracking files (these are workflow overhead, not operations)
Decision flow or template file reads
operation_counter_definition.tracking_instruction: LLM agents MUST increment operation counter in working_memory.json or step_progress_tracker.json after each operation

validation_before_every_operation: CRITICAL_FIRST: STOP and verify pwd equals /path/to/reflow/systems/<system_name> BEFORE ANY other operation
CRITICAL_FIRST: If pwd is wrong, execute recovery procedure immediately - DO NOT PROCEED
READ: context/current_focus.md (MUST be in current system's context/ directory)
READ: context/step_progress_tracker.json (MUST be in current system's context/ directory)
VERIFY: Your planned action matches current_step/substep in step_progress_tracker.json
VERIFY: Your planned action aligns with decision_flow.json instructions for this step
VERIFY: system_name from working_memory.json matches <system_name> in pwd
CONFIRM: No files from other systems will be modified
CONFIRM: You are NOT about to generate a report or summary
NOTE: ALL tracking files are ALWAYS in systems/<system_name>/context/ - NEVER in root or other directories
refresh_sequence: VERIFY PWD: Run 'pwd' and confirm you are in /path/to/reflow/systems/<system_name>
SAVE: Update context/step_progress_tracker.json and context/working_memory.json IN CURRENT SYSTEM DIRECTORY
RELOAD: ../../decision_flow.json (from system directory) - RE-READ CRITICAL_BEHAVIORAL_RULES AND CRITICAL_FILE_LOCATIONS section
READ: context/current_focus.md (in current system directory: pwd must be systems/<system_name>)
READ: context/step_progress_tracker.json (in current system directory: pwd must be systems/<system_name>)
VERIFY: Next action aligns with decision_flow.json instructions for current step
CONFIRM: State system name, step, substep, next action
CONFIRM: Next action does NOT involve generating a report
CRITICAL: All context/ files referenced above are relative to systems/<system_name>/ directory
REMINDER: If you lose track of file locations after this refresh, re-read CRITICAL_FILE_LOCATIONS section at top of decision_flow.json
degradation_signals: Asking about system name when it's in working_memory.json
pwd does not match system_name from working_memory.json
Generating reports or summaries after completing steps
Taking actions that contradict decision_flow.json instructions
Acting as if decision_flow.json guidance is optional

tracking_files.CRITICAL_LOCATION_RULE: ALL tracking files MUST be in systems/<system_name>/context/ directory. NO EXCEPTIONS.
tracking_files.note: All tracking files are in the context/ folder for LLM agent workflow guidance
reinforcement: NEVER look for tracking files in reflow root directory

ALWAYS use relative paths from current system directory: context/<filename>
IF you cannot find a tracking file, you are likely in the WRONG DIRECTORY - check pwd immediately
ARCHITECTURE workflow uses: current_focus.md, step_progress_tracker.json, working_memory.json
DEVELOPMENT workflow uses: dev_current_focus.md, dev_progress_tracker.json, dev_working_memory.json

system_isolation_recovery.description: Procedure when wrong-system context is detected
triggers: pwd does not match system_name from working_memory.json
Attempting to access files from other system directories
Creating files with paths containing different system names
Any degradation signal related to wrong system context
recovery_steps: STOP immediately - Do not create/modify any more files
Document the error in current directory's context/process_log.md with timestamp
Identify correct system name from user's request or previous conversation context
READ context/working_memory.json to reestablish context (file is in current directory's context/ subdirectory)
READ context/current_focus.md to understand current task (file is in current directory's context/ subdirectory)
RESUME work with verified context and document recovery
REMEMBER: Tracking files are ALWAYS at context/<filename> relative to systems/<system_name>/ directory

correct_approach: pwd  # Verify correct directory - should show /path/to/reflow/systems/<system_name>
ls context/  # Verify context directory exists with tracking files
cat context/current_focus.md  # Read context from current system (or dev_current_focus.md for development)
cat context/step_progress_tracker.json  # Check progress (or dev_progress_tracker.json for development)
All file operations relative to current directory
NEVER use absolute paths that might point to wrong system
wrong_approach_avoid: ❌ Working in wrong directory without verification
❌ Reading context files from other systems

from_system_directory.note: Use '.' for system_path argument when already in system directory

generate_interface_contracts.issue: Tool requires index.json in system root directory
generate_interface_contracts.note: Cleanup index.json after generation to maintain clean structure

system_of_systems_graph.requirement: Must be run from system directory for relative path resolution

tool_invocation_standards.recommended_practice: Use 'from_system_directory' pattern for all manual operations. Ensures pwd verification and system isolation are maintained.

validate_architecture.purpose: Validate service_architecture.json files for template compliance and architectural consistency
validate_architecture.output_format: JSON with validation results categorized by check type (interface_consistency, resource_isolation, dependency_cycles)

file_location_requirements.note: Tool uses rglob to find service_architecture.json files recursively - works with reflow's specs-based structure

llm_agent_workflow: 1. Parse validation results JSON to identify failed checks and specific issues
2. Address interface issues by updating service_architecture.json files in specs/machine/service_arch/
3. Fix resource isolation problems by ensuring proper service boundaries
4. Resolve dependency cycles by refactoring service responsibilities
5. Create missing service_architecture.json files in specs/machine/service_arch/ for incomplete services
6. Re-run validation until all checks pass with zero issues
issue_types_detected: interface_missing: Service interfaces not found in interface_registry.json
interface_mismatch: Service interface definitions don't match registry
circular_dependency: Services have cyclic dependencies that prevent startup
shared_resource: Multiple services access same resources without isolation
prerequisites: System must follow reflow directory structure with specs/ and services/ separation

system_of_systems_graph.purpose: Generate machine-readable system graph and detect architectural issues for LLM analysis

output_files.graph_json: NetworkX node_link_data format with nodes (services/systems) and links (interfaces/dependencies)
output_files.issues_json: Structured architectural issues with severity levels and specific recommendations

llm_agent_workflow: 1. Parse issues_json to identify problems requiring immediate attention
2. Analyze graph_json to understand system topology and data flow
3. Cross-reference with service_architecture.json files to understand issue context
4. Apply specific fixes based on issue type and recommendations
5. Update service definitions and interfaces to resolve architectural problems
6. Re-run tool until no critical/warning issues remain
issue_types_detected: circular_dependencies: Services that depend on each other in cycles
orphaned_nodes: Services with no connections (potential dead code)
inconsistent_protocols: Services mixing too many communication patterns
prerequisites: index.json with 'components' key mapping service_id to file paths

generate_interface_contracts.purpose: Generate complete Interface Contract Documents (ICDs) from service architectures for independent development

output_files.individual_icds: interfaces/<interface_id>.json files with complete contract specifications
output_files.interfaces_summary: interfaces/interfaces_summary.json with overview of all contracts

llm_development_workflow: 1. Use generated ICD files as authoritative interface specifications during development
2. Implement provider components to satisfy output_specification requirements
3. Implement consumer components to send requests matching input_specification
4. Use integration_tests scenarios to verify component contract compliance
5. Follow error_handling specifications for robust error management
6. Generated contracts guarantee integration success when followed precisely
contract_elements_provided: input_specification: Complete schemas and constraints for interface inputs
output_specification: Expected response formats and success criteria
error_handling: Error conditions, responses, and retry policies
timing_constraints: Performance requirements and synchronization needs
integration_tests: Test scenarios to verify contract compliance

llm_usage_instructions: Parse feature summary document to identify distinct system boundaries
Extract system requirements from feature descriptions
Populate working memory with required systems for architecture design

Ensure all features are mapped to appropriate system responsibilities

verify_component_contract.purpose: Verify component implementations satisfy contracts and specifications for guaranteed integration success

Use compliance score to assess component readiness

Only integrate components that pass contract verification

critical_file_dependencies: index.json LOCATION: Primary location is systems/<system_name>/specs/machine/index.json with portable relative paths
index.json MUST have 'components' key mapping service_id to relative paths like 'specs/machine/service_arch/<service>/service_architecture.json'
interface_registry.json MUST be in specs/machine/ for validate_architecture.py
service_architecture.json files MUST be in specs/machine/service_arch/<service_name>/ NOT in services/<service_name>/
This separation maintains clean division: specs/ for architecture, services/ for implementation code
Tool workaround: For generate_interface_contracts.py, temporarily copy specs/machine/index.json to system root, then remove after generation
AVOID: specs/index.json with absolute paths (not portable for git clones)
Both files must be created during architecture workflow before validation
Use index_template.json and interface_registry_template.json for correct formats
